claim: Flanders' fietsknooppunten system assigns numbers to network intersections so cyclists string nodes together to design routes, signed by rectangular markers.
quote: Where two or more routes intersect, this is called a node... simply cycle along, following the signs from node to numbered node, with rectangular signs marking each node.

claim: Visit Bruges promotes the Bruges-to-Damme canal ride and signed cycling node loops as the main cycling product around the city.
The Bruges-Damme tow-path along the Damse Vaart is roughly 7 km one-way, flat, lined with poplars, and family-friendly.
quote: The ride is about 7 kilometers one way, making it accessible for all levels and even suitable for families.

claim: Kasteel van Loppem at Steenbrugsestraat 26, Zedelgem-Loppem opens to individuals March to mid-November, Mon-Sat 13:00-17:30 with adult tickets at €12 and a separate hedge maze at €11.
quote: Monday to Saturday, 13:00-17:30... Adults (18+) €12... Maze €11... Steenbrugsestraat 26, 8210 Zedelgem-Loppem

claim: Loppem Castle is a Gothic Revival residence built 1859-1862 by E.W. Pugin and J.-B. de Béthune that served as King Albert I's residence 24 October-25 November 1918, where the Loppem Agreements led to universal male suffrage; it has been a museum under the Jean van Caloen Foundation since 1975.
quote: the castle served as the residence of Albert I of Belgium from 24 October until 25 November 1918... has functioned as a museum since 1975

claim: Tillegembos Provincial Domain covers about 144 hectares of mixed deciduous-coniferous forest, heath, grassland and orchards on Bruges' green outskirts, with trails fanning out from Tillegem Castle.
quote: extensive natural beauty across its 144 hectares, providing varied landscapes that feature a mix of dense forests, heathlands, grasslands, and orchards

claim: The 'Three Castles Route' south of Bruges links Tillegem, Tudor and Beisbroek castle estates on a single signed walk, and an unpaved trail crosses Beisbroek forest past the public observatory.
quote: the Three Castles Route starts south of Bruges and takes hikers past the castles in Tillegem, Tudor and Beisbroek

claim: Cozmix / Volkssterrenwacht Beisbroek at Zeeweg 96, 8200 Brugge runs a planetarium with 7,000+ projected stars plus a telescope tower; admission is €8 adult / €6 child 4-17 / free under 4.
quote: Adults: €8.00 Children (4-17): €6.00... more than seven thousand stars projected onto the interior of the dome

claim: Cozmix opens to individuals from 17:30 with planetarium shows at 18:00 and 19:00 and monthly Friday 'Space 4 Kids' family observation evenings October-April.
quote: open from 5:30 p.m., with planetarium shows at 6 p.m. and 7 p.m... monthly (from October to April) family nocturnes on Friday evenings called 'Space 4 Kids'

claim: Provinciedomein Lippensgoed-Bulskampveld in Beernem (about 20 km from Bruges) hosts bike and XL-game hire, a renovated playground, a castle with a 'Roots' exhibition and a 2026 spring activities programme for families and adults.
quote: You can hire bicycles or XL-games and discover the renewed playground. The domain also features a castle with an 'Roots' exhibition.

claim: Kasteel van Male in Sint-Kruis traces to a 9th-century anti-Viking tower; rebuilt after WWII, it housed St. Trudo's Abbey 1954-2011 before being sold to a private owner in 2011, with the sisters relocating in 2013.
quote: have housed St. Trudo's Abbey (Sint-Trudoabdij) from 1954 until 2011. In 2011 the sisters... sold the abbey at Male to a private individual

claim: The Grafelijk Slot van Male site in Sint-Kruis now operates as a St. Trudo Abbey visitors' centre via the Brugse Ommeland tourism network rather than a full castle tour.
quote: Grafelijk Slot van Male - Kasteel van Male

claim: Visit Bruges lists multiple official bicycle rental points across the city for tourists planning day rides on the node network.
Ben's Bike at 't Zand rents city bikes at €4/hour, €10/half-day (5h) and €13/full day.
quote: Ben's Bike offers city bikes at €4/hour, €10/half day (5 hours), and €13/full day
